question.worked_solution:
Recall that the equation of an elliptic cone centered at $O$ whose axis of symmetry is the $z$-axis is given by

$$
\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

Thus, an elliptic cone centered at $O$ whose axis of symmetry is the $y$**-axis** is given by

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, our equation is an elliptic cone whose axis of symmetry is the $y$-axis and $b=\sqrt{5},\,a=c=\sqrt{2}.$
